Tokyo —
Christopher Payne’s dream was to build a life in Japan.
As a 12-year-old in Indiana, he fell in love with the country through anime, spending hours watching Pokémon on YouTube. He taught himself Japanese and eventually became fluent. In 2013, he started living in Japan, first to teach English and then to work for one of Japan’s biggest internet companies.
But in 2021, his dreams were dashed. He was arrested for sexual assault—a crime he maintains he didn’t commit—and sentenced to eight years in prison for a conviction that has since been overturned. A high court ordered a retrial, but no date has been set.
Despite no charge against him, Payne remains behind bars, a punishment the now 34-year-old described to CNN as “purgatory.”

Iran must address its declining population by encouraging young people to marry and have children, according to Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei.
The country of 93 million faces a demographic crisis, with an aging population and falling birthrate as young couples struggle to afford homes and start families amid a deepening economic slump.
In a statement attributed to him on Tuesday, Khamenei said Iran must address shortcomings in past population policies, describing population growth as a “strategic priority.”
His message was read at a ceremony for the National Population Rejuvenation Award, which honors efforts to help families and increase Iran’s birth rate.
